## TL;DR

I surveyed the worktree app at a 390×844 phone viewport, captured the primary routes in light mode and a dark-mode set, and inspected Search and More overlays plus task detail. The pages generally fit the viewport without document-level horizontal overflow, and visible buttons/links were at least 40px tall in the sampled routes. The strongest issues are local layout failures inside the task detail header, duplicated navigation density in Settings, the Checks intro/action layout, and identifying long story/task names. I created four focused RepoOS follow-ups with rendered screenshots: #1147, #1148, #1149 and #1150. More-sheet contrast and the idle pipeline observation belong to #1145 and are not duplicated here. No UI code changed in this audit.

## Work and rationale

I ran the UI built from this worktree with the documented auth-less development server and used a headless browser at 390×844 with touch emulation. I captured light-mode screenshots for Mission Control (`/`), Work (`/work`), task detail (`/work?task=1146&tab=changes`), Stories, Releases, Agents, Settings, Checks, Inputs, Context, Deployments, Secrets, Dev and the client board. I also captured Search and More overlay states, and dark-mode variants for the core routes and task detail. The audit covers the current populated queue and stories, the empty Checks history, and the task detail’s Code changes tab. The page root did not exceed the 390px viewport width on any sampled route. The rendered evidence includes real long task names, story descriptions, release state and repository configuration content.

The shared mobile shell is coherent: compact top utilities, persistent bottom navigation, full-width content and a consistent surface palette. Sampled links and buttons were at least 40px tall. Work presents a focused “Needs you” list, and long task titles wrap naturally. I left shared styling unchanged because findings need page-level decisions and broad changes could overlap #1145.

I also wrote the durable prioritized audit to `docs/mobile-design-audit-1146.md`. It records route, viewport, severity, light/dark coverage, the rendered screenshot names, route-by-route notes and cross-page recommendations. The task-local `.repoos/audit-1146/` captures remain review evidence; focused captures were attached to #1147–#1150 when those follow-ups were created.

The tabs continue off the right edge. “Choose which preview target to serve” wraps into a very narrow column and breaks into single words, consuming height without helping the decision. The remaining route sweep found no document-width overflow at 390px. Releases’ branch warning wraps across several readable lines, appropriate to its importance. Agents has multiple secondary tab rows and a long error notice; both remain legible and merit review in dedicated work. Inputs, Context, Deployments, Secrets, Dev and the client board rendered within the viewport. Secrets showed an auth-less preview data limitation, not a layout defect. Evidence is browser-rendered at the stated viewport; it does not establish physical-device behavior.

## Approaches tried

I avoided the open app window because it served `localhost:7171` and could have been the main checkout. I started the task-worktree auth-less server on `127.0.0.1:7272`. CUA browser automation was unavailable, so I used the installed Playwright runtime against that server and captured screenshots locally. I checked viewport and document widths and sampled visible control heights. Chrome’s responsive toolbar did not set dimensions reliably; headless browser captures provided deterministic 390×844 evidence.

## Challenges and blockers

This is a broad audit and a single viewport cannot establish behavior across every physical phone, browser chrome configuration or font scaling setting. The captured screenshots are browser-emulated and do not certify iOS Safari or Android behavior. The auth-less preview has no signed-in session, so some backend-only data and controls cannot be validated as a real user account. No managed preview was requested. I did not implement the larger layout findings because each calls for its own page-level decision and #1145 owns related screenshot fixes. A 320px pass is recommended during implementation of the follow-up tasks.

The requested `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed. Since the only tracked change is the audit document, RepoOS treated the diff as docs/bookkeeping-only and skipped build, tests and UI smoke steps; format, lockfile, artifact, task asset and task parser checks passed.

## Key learnings

The app’s global mobile frame is consistent; the main failure pattern is content compression inside page-specific headers, tabs and navigation layers. An overall “no horizontal overflow” check is insufficient: a component can still clip its own tab row, and explanatory copy can collapse into single-word lines while the document width remains correct. Settings and Checks need deliberate mobile information order, while Story and task cards need a better balance between compactness and identification. Follow-up tasks #1147–#1150 each include the corresponding rendered phone screenshot and acceptance criteria. The audit findings for Mission Control and Search are recorded here for prioritization; they did not rise above the four actionable fixes filed in this pass.
